---
name: requirements
description: "Turn a user story into clear requirements and acceptance criteria that a person can approve. Use at the start of an SDLC cycle."
argument-hint: "User story or source document"
---

# Requirements

1. Read the story. Note who it is for, what they want, why, and any acceptance criteria already written.
2. Open any file the story points to. If it mentions Jira, Confluence or a document you were not given, say you can't see it rather than guess.
3. Ask a question when the answer would change scope, security, storage, how tests run, or how success is measured. Skip the rest.
4. Keep four lists apart: facts from the story, decisions the user approved, assumptions you are proposing, and questions still open.
5. Write `requirements.md`: the story, functional and non-functional requirements, acceptance criteria, constraints, assumptions, and what is out of scope.
6. Check that each acceptance criterion can be observed and tested, and give it an ID others can refer to.
7. Show the draft and wait for the user to approve it before architecture starts.

Don't answer questions on the stakeholders' behalf, and don't build the feature in this phase.
